entries.mechanism:
Massachusetts's broad-based categorical eligibility (SNAP state option;
PolicyEngine models gross screen x2.0 FPL, x2.0 for elderly/disabled
households, at 2026-01 per gov/hhs/tanf/non_cash parameters) is not in
the composed us-ma/snap/fy-2026 program, which applies only the standard
federal tests. Every selected row is verified per-row against axiom's
persisted output surface: household gross income sits inside the band
above the federal 130 percent limit the composed program applies and at
or below the state's BBCE screen, verified against axiom's own computed
gross income and limit. Axiom-side modeling boundary, tracked for
encoding in rulespec-us#1098.

Reverified on PolicyEngine 4.18.9, PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3, and PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The exact-household signature and explicit K-12 counterfactual reproduce the mechanism: PolicyEngine excludes all earnings of an imputed K-12 member age 17 or younger without requiring the co-resident-parent or parental-control condition in 7 CFR 273.9(c)(7). The sole minor is a valid household under 273.1(a)(1), but wages count under 273.9(b)(1)(i), so Axiom correctly fails the income gate and returns zero benefit. The requested-month replay retains the same benefit and eligibility rows; the benefit comparison is now Axiom 0.0 versus PolicyEngine 298.0 (the January allotment), replacing the old annual-average 299.66998291015625.

Exact-household live counterfactual on PolicyEngine 4.18.9, PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3, and PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3: the regenerated baseline is Axiom 693.0 versus PE 379.6999816894531. PE reports January ma_tafdc 698.7846069335938 and calendar-year TANF 8385.4150390625. Forcing both to zero leaves SNAP eligibility true and produces January PE SNAP 694.0999755859375; its absolute delta from Axiom is 1.0999755859375, within the suite tolerance 7.0. This exact counterfactual isolates endogenous TANF transport as the mismatch mechanism.
